title: dactylorhiza incarnata subsp. pulchella
intro: Dactylorhiza incarnata subsp. pulchella, commonly known as the crimson helleborine, is a sub-species of orchid native to Europe, characterized by its bright pink flowers and distinctive growth habit. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Dactylorhiza incarnata subsp. pulchella include wound healing, anti-arthritic, and anti-diabetic effects, attributed to its bioactive constituents such as phenolic acids, flavonoids, and terpenoids. Studies have identified the bioactive constituents of this plant, which include phenolic acids, flavonoids, and terpenoids, contributing to its therapeutic properties.
